+#### Advanced Table Extraction — one table spanning multiple pages
+**A table that continues across pages usually repeats its header only on the FIRST
+page.** The continuation pages start straight into data with no header row. So you must
+take the header ONCE and treat every row on later pages as data.
+**Do NOT strip `table[1:]` on every page** and do NOT build from `tables[0]` alone —
+both silently drop the first data row of each continuation page (and `tables[0]`-only
+ignores every later page entirely). This is a classic off-by-one that loses one employee
+/ record per page and is a frequent cause of "count is short by N" bugs.
-            if table:  # Check if table is not empty
+                header = tbl[0]          # header appears once, on the first table
+                # continuation page: NO repeated header -> keep ALL rows,
+                # only skip a row if it is literally a repeat of the header.
+                rows.extend(r for r in tbl if r != header)
+# df now has every data row; count == number of records in the source table.
+If different tables on the page are genuinely separate (each with its own header),
+handle them per-table instead — the rule above is specifically for ONE logical table

+### Positioning and centering a shape on the slide
+Two things are independent and BOTH are needed when a task says "center":

+1. **Text alignment inside the box** is set per paragraph via `<a:pPr algn="ctr"/>`, which must be the **first child of every `<a:p>`** in the shape. Moving the box does NOT center the text — without `algn="ctr"` the text stays left-aligned. Values: `l` (left, default), `ctr`, `r`, `just`.
+2. **Horizontal position of the box** is set by `<a:off x=.. y=..>` inside `<p:spPr>/<a:xfrm>`. To center the box horizontally, `x = (slide_width - shape_width) // 2`.

+**CRITICAL — read the real slide size; never assume it.** Slide width/height live in `ppt/presentation.xml` as `<p:sldSz cx=".." cy=".."/>`. Modern 16:9 decks are `cx="12192000" cy="6858000"` EMU; the older 4:3 default is `cx="9144000"`. Hardcoding 9144000 / "10 inches" is the most common centering bug — it mis-centers every 16:9 deck. For **bottom center**, keep the centered `x` and set `y = slide_height - shape_height - bottom_margin`.

+When a task asks for a **PivotTable** (or "pivot table"), it means a genuine native Excel PivotTable — the `xl/pivotTables/*.xml` + `xl/pivotCache/*` parts that Excel and graders inspect for row/column/value fields and aggregation.
+- **openpyxl CANNOT create a PivotTable** with its high-level API (`from openpyxl.pivot.table import PivotTable` does not exist / there is no create method).

+- **Do NOT fake it** by writing a pandas `groupby`/`crosstab` result into plain cells. A manual summary table looks similar but has NO pivotTable part, so it fails any check that reads the pivot configuration.
